extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, Royal Society members, and 17th-century scientific authors/experimenters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for preparing and presenting natural-philosophy (mathematical, anatomical, botanical, and physical) papers for a learned society: includes how to construct proofs, present experiments, provide figures, and justify claims by repeated observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present general methods and multiple constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: His general methods for finding two means, by a circle and either an hyperbola or ellipsis, are laid down in Prop. 1,2,16; he shows many methods and infinite such effectioiis, not in one method but many.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give both general method(s) and demonstrate that they produce many particular constructions; enumerate propositions and show how general methods handle classes of problems (e.g., solving cubic equations, doubling the cube, trisection of angles). Show extent and variety of the methods (many infinite ways).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide the algebraic/analytical basis for geometric constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the second part of his book De Analysi, the author first gives the analysis or algebra, whereby all his general methods of finding two means were invented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the analysis that invents the constructions and relate algebraic reasoning to the geometric procedures; show how algebra informs particular constructions and the invention of delineations for equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show both general constructions and particular illustrative cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular effectiions for finding out one or both of the means, and doubling the cube in prop. 3 to 6; then further examples from prop. 7 to 12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alongside general proofs, supply worked examples/propositions demonstrating particular cases (e.g., specific constructions for one or both means, examples of trisection), and use these to exhibit the method's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use accurate figures/illustrations to elucidate arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole receives a singular elucidation and ornament by the accurate figures annexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear, accurate plates/figures demonstrating constructions and experimental setup; figures should clarify arguments and aid replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin anatomical/physiological accounts with precise structure descriptions linked to function
rubrics_metrics.description: He begins with a discourse concerning the situation and structure of the heart, to show how exactly these two are calculated for its motion, and how well adapted to distribute the blood into the parts of the whole body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide minute description of organs (parts, nerves, vessels), explain mechanical contrivance (systole/diastole), and connect anatomy to physiological function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base physiological claims on experiments and rebut alternative explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: He proves by experiments, and vindicates from objections; refuting withal the opinion of those that attribute it to the comminution of the blood in the lungs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support assertions with experiments, give experimental evidence against rival hypotheses, and explicitly address objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify physiological phenomena where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: He calculates that all the blood passes through the body 13 times in one hour; considers the quantity of that liquor emitted at every pulsation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numerical estimates and calculations (rates, quantities) derived from observation and experiment; correct for errors and report measurement methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design botanical/physiological experiments with controlled, repeatable procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: For completing the experiment on sap... let the tree, exhausted of all its sap the day before, be first pierced with an auger... the quantity of sap it yields exactly measured and weighed: then at the same time let another hole be bored into the body... and so round on every side of the same tree, and of others of the same sort...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control initial conditions (e.g., exhaust sap day before), standardize procedures (depths of holes, tools used), measure quantitatively (weigh sap), vary one factor at a time (hole depth, bark vs inner wood), and repeat trials across multiple trees of same sort for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use replication and varying conditions to distinguish effects
rubrics_metrics.description: From this experiment, after divers and various trials, may be found the difference of the sap rising on the north and south, in sun and shade, and so likewise from that which comes from the bark, and that which ascends in the inner part of the tree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run diverse and repeated trials, compare across environmental conditions (north/south, sun/shade), and compare sources (bark vs inner tissues) to attribute observed differences confidently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe detailed, practical procedures for collection, fermentation, and preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve sap in the best condition for brewing; what is drawn first must be constantly exposed to the sun in glasses... then put into it so much very thin cut and hard toasted, but no ways burned, rye-bread, as will serve to ferment it; and when it works take out the bread, and bottle the liquor, stopping it up with waxed corks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precise procedural instructions (timings, materials like toasted rye-bread not burned, use of cloves, toasted herbs, spirit of wine, bottling and stoppers) so others can reproduce preserved brews; note variants and expected outcomes (e.g., cloves preserve for 12 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend horticultural interventions with rationale and method
rubrics_metrics.description: To make a barren tree bear again; nourish it with dung in trenches, and pare and renew the extremities of its longest roots, and cut off the outermost and shortest nearest the body... Cross hackings promote fruitfulness, and cure the phyllomania or luxuriancy of leaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide both the practical steps (cross hackings, pruning, ablaqueation, cleaving roots and inserting a stone) and the physiological rationale (redirecting sap from wood to fruit), including cautions about doing both stem and roots for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare competing theories and prefer those agreeing with repeated observation
rubrics_metrics.description: On comparing their several sentiments on this subject, that theory might be adopted which should be found to agree best with observation and experiment, carefully made and often repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple theoretical accounts exist (Galileo, Descartes, Fabri, etc.), actively compare them against careful, repeated observations and experiments; select and promote the theory best supported by empirical evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect authorship and archival/copyright norms when publishing discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society ordered, after first obtaining the permission of the authors to publish these discoveries, that they might be more conveniently communicated... it was not thought proper to publish his discoveries, especially as they were not then entire. In the meantime... they should be laid up in the public archives of the Royal Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain author consent before publishing their discoveries, avoid premature publication of incomplete work without consent, deposit communications in public archives, and solicit authors to publish in appropriate journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely disclosure to establish priority and credit
rubrics_metrics.description: M. Huygens was wanting to himself in delaying that publication, thus giving occasion to Dr. Wren... to claim a just title to some share of the glory of the discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish or communicate discoveries in a timely manner (or deposit them in archives/correspondence) to secure priority and avoid disputes over independent discovery; keep correspondence and records to document claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulate physical laws with clear assumptions, numbered rules, and demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules concerning the Motion of Bodies after mutual Impulse... (1) If a hard body strike against another and equal hard body, at rest; after impact the former will rest, and the latter will acquire a velocity equal to that of the moving body. ... (6) The sum of the products arising from multiplying the mass of each hard body into the square of its velocity, is the same both before and after the stroke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State laws as clear, enumerated rules, supply geometric/analytic demonstrations and diagrams (e.g., fig. 4, pl. 9), and specify the operative assumptions (e.g., bodies 'hard' meaning elastic, homogeneity or mass estimated by weight). Note derived surprising laws (e.g., uniform motion of common centre of gravity) and their domain of applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparative mechanical reasoning across species to infer general principles
rubrics_metrics.description: He considers the diversity of the situation of the heart in different animals, and the reason thereof; proving further, that the substance of the heart is perfectly muscular, and in perfection surpassing all other muscles of the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare anatomy across taxa, reason by mechanical analogy (muscle action, fibres, nerves) to derive general physiological principles, and support such inferences with observation and experiment.
